text:
ellie: heads up — saw a spike where a single org consumed burst credits and then started getting 503s from the soft-queue, while other keys were still idle. wondering if our shedding signals are leaking useful info to clients
kevin: ugh. which path returned 503 vs 429? iirc soft-queue fallback returns 503 and precheck immediate rejects return 429
maria: correct. precheck quota fail -> 429, soft-queue eviction -> 503. but clients can only show one message so we need consistent UX
ellie: proposal: include X-Redwood-Shed-Reason header with values like "precheck_quota", "soft_queue_evicted", "burst_depleted" so clients can decide whether to retry or switch behavior
jason: +1. also surface a short machine-readable JSON body: {"error":"rate_limited","reason":"soft_queue_evicted","retry_after":10} for easy handling
kevin: prefer header + simple body. less parsing at SDK layer. we should define exact header names and semantics. also if we leak "soft_queue_evicted" it might reveal capacity issues — is that ok?
maria: it's internal platform; customers need guidance. we can include higher-level categories: "throttled" vs "unavailable" as well as a more detailed header for SDKs behind the scenes
ops-bot: note: we already emit metric redwood_shed_total{reason=...,org=...,key=...} in prometheus. If we add header let's also emit a counter for header_exposed_total to track customer-facing signals
ellie: telemetry ask: add a label for severity (soft/early/forced) and for downstream action (retryable/non_retryable) so console can show "safe to retry" flags
jason: UI/console change: per-key dashboard should show current burst credits, burst recharge rate, and a small "last shed reason" sparkline per key. PM liked this idea in roadmap sync
kevin: implementation detail: precheck runs at gateway and is O(1). soft-queue eviction happens at router after queuing attempt. header should be set by the component that actually decided. propagate through proxy via X-Redwood-Shed-Reason and X-Redwood-Retry-After
maria: sample error response we can standardize:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
X-Redwood-Shed-Reason: soft_queue_evicted
X-Redwood-Retry-After: 12
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"service_unavailable","reason":"soft_queue_evicted","retry_after_seconds":12}
```
kevin: what about 429 responses from precheck? should include Retry-After and indicate burst credits remaining = 0
ellie: yes. 429 body example:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-Shed-Reason: precheck_quota
X-Redwood-Burst-Credits: 0
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"rate_limited","reason":"precheck_quota","burst_credits":0,"retry_after_seconds":30}
```
maria: ops ask: make sure we don't create alert noise. If we expose header_exposed_total we can create a dashboard that shows customer-visible sheds vs internal evictions and only alert on sustained increase in customer-visible sheds
jason: rollout plan: feature flag at gateway+router to start emitting headers. SDKs can opt-in to read them. Console will show data once metric is emitted. Start behind ff for 10% of traffic for 2 days then roll
kevin: compatibility: older SDKs ignore unknown headers, so opt-in is safe. add migration note in changelog and API release notes
ellie: one more: add a human-friendly mapping in docs so support can tell customers: precheck_quota -> "hit quota, try again later or request higher quota"; soft_queue_evicted -> "transient capacity issue, please retry with backoff"
maria: ok I'll open a tiny RFC with the header names, body schema, metrics to emit, and rollout plan. will add sample queries for console panels and prometheus rules
jason: sounds good. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: gateway ff toggle will be created in config repo (pr opened by maria)
rate-limiter-bot: metric created: redwood_shed_header_exposed_total (labels: reason,org,key,severity)
ellie: thanks everyone — let's sync in eng-standup if any blockers show up before rollout
